title: Specification Oracles
abstract: arXiv:2609.13415v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Specifications face a basic tradeoff: leave details out, and important questions go unanswered; record every detail separately, and the specification becomes large and prolix. We investigate whether a language model can serve as a compact, living specification oracle by learning facts about a target and answering questions about it directly. We compare two ways of storing the learned facts: external text notes and changes to the model's weights. Across four families of 596-fact worlds and two Qwen2.5 model sizes, weight-only oracles benefited substantially more from structure: with the 7B model, their accuracy integrated across storage capacities was 18.5 percentage points higher on structured than unstructured worlds, compared with 1.1 points for note-sheet oracles. translated_abstract: 规范面临一个基本的权衡：省略细节会导致重要问题无从解答，而将每个细节都单独记录又会使规范变得庞大冗长。我们研究语言模型能否充当一种紧凑的、动态的“规范神谕”——通过学习关于目标的事实并直接回答相关问题。我们比较了两种存储所学事实的方式：外部文本笔记与对模型权重的修改。在四个包含596个事实的世界家族以及两种Qwen2.5模型规模上，仅权重型神谕从结构化信息中获益显著更多：使用7B模型时，其在存储容量上的综合准确率在结构化世界中比非结构化世界高出18.5个百分点，而笔记式神谕仅高出1.1个百分点。但这一优势伴随着可观的存储成本：最小的适配器约需175 KiB，而笔记的最大预算仅为16 KiB。适配后的权重……（摘要原文截断）
tldr: 本研究提出让语言模型充当紧凑的“规范神谕”，发现通过修改权重存储事实的方式在结构化知识上远优于外部笔记（准确率高18.5个百分点），但代价是需要更多的存储空间。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes using language models as compact "specification oracles," finding that storing facts via weight adaptation far outperforms external notes on structured worlds (18.5 vs. 1.1 percentage points accuracy gain), though at a substantially higher storage cost.
